name: Read me
values: Completed saved research through 30 September 2026. Includes negative results, calibration-only work and older corrected channel runs. No new training in this report.
Within each comparison, keep real assessment observations, years, timestamps, annotations and event scope fixed. Select checkpoints and alarm settings using training/calibration only.

Assessment uses real ESA telemetry after the documented preprocessing and real event annotations. Synthetic anomalies occur in training only. Masked inference hides observed input patches but scores real target values.
Current main model sees channels 40–47. System scoring checks events across all 76 telemetry channels. Local scoring checks annotations on channels 40–47.
2003, 2004 and 2005 each mean April–December assessment. Training uses earlier years. Calibration uses January–March of that year. These periods were inspected previously.
Train 2000–2005. Calibrate 2006. Assess all months of 2007–2013 with a frozen rule. Annual rows are slices of those same predictions.
Compare within a named comparison group and matching event scope. Same years alone do not control training budget, initialization, preprocessing, information access or checkpoint selection.
Blank numeric cells mean unavailable or not reported, never zero. Methods without 2007–2013 results have not yet been evaluated under the full-period protocol.
The historical audit uses existing weights and corrected metrics. It includes a final 2014-01-01 boundary sample. Original checkpoint selection and training splits differ from current runs.
Full-period baseline: local F0.5 0.8629066303 and system F0.5 0.8057217337. The system target ≥0.85 is not robustly achieved.
Each chart identifies a common assessment period. Modified augmentation averages three seeds. The no-short-roll follow-up has only seed 42. No best-seed selection.
esa-ew-id-duration-v1. Corrected event precision P = TP/(TP+FP) × (1 − false-positive nominal seconds/nominal seconds). R = TP/(TP+FN). F0.5 = 1.25PR/(0.25P+R).
TP = detected event IDs, FN = missed event IDs, FP = unmatched predicted events. Event counts across yearly slices can overlap and need not sum to pooled counts.
Calibration F0.5 chooses settings. Assessment F0.5 reports performance after freezing settings. Calibration-only results never substitute for assessment.
Repeatedly inspected development and benchmark periods are exploratory evidence, not a new untouched test. Retrospective reconstruction is not a demonstrated real-time operational detector.
Result rows link to source IDs. Sources lists run/artifact identifiers and SHA-256 hashes. The workbook preserves reported metrics and does not retrain or alter historical predictions.

Keep fixed real assessment folds and protocols. Finish planned seeds 43/44 before considering promotion. Any later full-period comparison needs the same 2000–2005 / 2006 / 2007–2013 split and a matched baseline.

name: Method guide
values: Normal reconstruction plus synthetic-anomaly separation loss
Learn normal patterns and make corruptions score higher
Low reconstruction loss did not guarantee high F0.5
Baseline alarm OR optional specialist alarm, gated by calibration
Catch events missed by either detector
2003 false events increased1 to 6 without extra detections
Hide25% of temporal patches and reconstruct hidden targets
Learn relationships instead of copying visible values
Score hidden targets using overlap aggregation
Reduce score smearing from masked windows
50% legacy corruptions and 50% short30s–5min corruptions on 1–8 channels
Represent short events affecting multiple channels
Short branch uses offsets/noise only. Legacy branch keeps rolls
Avoid almost unchanged short shifts receiving an abnormal target
Add elapsed time since native observation and availability
Distinguish fresh observations from held values
Predict future values with persistence, MLP or Transformer
Center context on last observation and predict deviations
Require several threshold hits in a recent window
Fewer false events, sometimes fewer detections
Change calibration threshold candidates and nominal alarm constraint
Control alarm burden with the same model
Divide channel errors by training nominal q99 scales
Use timestep errors instead of whole-window mean
Historical paired assessment lower than window mean
Blocks, correlated groups, representatives and pseudo-anomaly variants

name: Full period
values: Train 2000–2005, calibrate 2006, assess 2007–2013. Eight input channels 40–47. Blank annual local scores were not saved in this baseline summary.

name: Timing comparison
values: Both arms use real observations and the same2007–2013 period. 5 epochs, all nominal windows. Compare this pair directly, not against the 40-epoch baseline.

name: Forecasts
values: Same real Apr–Dec2003 assessment. Causal forecasts have a 256-sample warmup and differ from retrospective reconstruction.

name: Alarm rules

name: OR combination

name: Historical scoring
values: Same historical model. Q4 2006 calibration. Real 2007–2013 assessment includes Jan 1,2014 boundary sample. This differs from the current half-open full-period protocol.
